findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed both a sanitizer bucket and the sanitizer dispenser to reach a concentration of 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- the line was ran for several minutes until air bubbles passed. Frequently monitor the concentration of chemicals used to sanitize food contact surfaces using test strips as recommended by the manufacturer's label (200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple food contact surfaces to contain an accumulation of debris:
1) Soda nozzles at the drive thru contain a significant accumulation of biofilm.
2) Soda nozzles at the self service station contain a significant accumulation of biofilm.
3) The ice scoop holder for the ice machine.
4) The lid of the soft serve machine.
CORRECTED- food contact surfaces were removed to be cleaned and sanitized at the triple sink. Discussed removing nozzles to be cleaned with a brush and sanitized daily. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris which may contaminate ready to eat foods and drinks.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the tongs above the fryer station to be stored between a tray and a shelf. CORRECTED- utensil storage was discussed with the PIC and other staff members, and tongs were laid flat on the tray. In use utensils shall be stored in a manner that prevents contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed duct tape above the men’s restroom hand sink and to the left of the walk in cooler. Duct tape contains adhesive that will deteriorate upon exposure to splash. Nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable. Remove duct tape and refinish areas the duct tape is covering.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are in need of repair:
1) FIRST REPEAT: Spray foam near the walk-in freezer/back door needs to be cut flush and painted to leave the surface smooth and easily cleanable.
2) There are broken tiles on either side of the mop sink.
Repair physical facilities to eliminate gaps and create smooth, easily cleanable surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: A food employee was observed wearing gloves to deliver food to customers in the dining room, return to the kitchen, and return to food preparation without washing hands or changing gloves. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who will review when to wash hands with employees. Ensure employees wash hands upon entering the kitchen prior to engaging in food preparation without washing.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: A food employee was observed rinsing a milkshake cup in the front counter handwashing sink. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who will review handsink use with employees. Ensure handsinks are ONLY used for handwashing, no other purpose.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Sticky fly strips were observed installed in several locations around the 3 compartment sink and clean dish storage. CORRECTED- PIC removed the fly strips and relocated them to use in the dry storage area. Fly strips may be put up overnight when no food is open in the kitchen.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Both the 3 compartment sink and the cookline handsink have leaks from the faucets. Repair sinks to eliminate the leaks.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are in need of repair:
1) Spray foam near the mop sink and walk-in freezer/back door needs to be cut flush and painted to leave the surface smooth and easily cleanable.
2) Broken floor tiles in front of the fryer need to be replaced.
3) Holes in the wall behind the 3 compartment sink need to be filled.
Repair physical facilities to eliminate gaps and create smooth, easily cleanable surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Current food handler certificates were not available for either of the two non-CFM employees present during this inspection (one is on file, but expired). Long John Silver’s is on the list of Illinois-approved food handler certificates, but PIC was unaware of this internal training and was unsure if staff have completed the course. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire, whether internally through Long John Silver’s or through another approved provider. 
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee wash hands then turn the faucet off without the use of a barrier. CORRECTED- Discussed proper handwashing procedure with the employee and PIC. Ensure a barrier is used to turn the faucet off and prevent recontamination of hands.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Food debris was observed on the blade of the can opener. CORRECTED- PIC removed the can opener to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Clean the can opener after each use.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
No ambient air thermometer was present in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC provided a thermometer and placed it near the entrance to the walk-in cooler. Ensure all cold holding units have thermometers in them.
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Soil accumulation observed on the wall behind the 3 compartment sink (around the wall-mounted detergent/sanitizer dispenser). Clean often enough to prevent accumulation.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
One food handler certificate was available on file. Long John Silver’s is on the list of Illinois-approved food handler certificates, but PIC was unaware of this internal training and unsure if staff have completed the course. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire, whether internally through Long John Silver’s, or through another approved provider.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
REPEAT: The ceiling is leaking along the front service counter, near the cash register, cold well, single-service storage, and fryers. Repair roof/ceiling to prevent leaks. Roofing was reported to be repaired after the previous visit. The facility is closed until the roof is repaired. Contact SCDPH for reinspection when the roof has been fixed for approval to reopen.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
The ceiling is leaking along the front service counter, near the cash register, cold well, single-service storage, and fryers. The leaks could easily contaminate single service containers or foods as they move through the kitchen. CORRECTED- The facility will cease food service until the leaks are repaired.
3-305.14: During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The ceiling is leaking along the front service counter, near the cash register, cold well, single-service storage, and fryers. Repair roof/ceiling to prevent leaks. Inspector will follow up in 2 weeks to see proof of repairs.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Bare wood is exposed on the end of the drive-thru soda fountain counter and where holes have been cut in the cabinet doors of the customer soda fountain. Paint or seal bare wood so it is protected from moisture. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Flies observed throughout the facility. Fly strips are used in non-food prep areas. Eliminate pests within the facility.
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. [Pf]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Two tubs of ice cream observed uncovered in the walk-in freezer. Keep ice cream covered to prevent potential contamination. CORRECTED- Lids added to containers.
3-305.14: During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Ice accumulation observed in the walk-in freezer in several locations. Eliminate accumulated ice and remove ice regularly to prevent accumulation, or repair so that ice does not develop.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Bare wood is exposed on the end of the drive-thru soda fountain counter and where holes have been cut in the cabinet doors of the customer soda fountain. Paint or seal bare wood so it is protected from moisture. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Soil accumulation observed on the wall behind the 3 compartment sink (around the wall-mounted detergent/sanitizer dispenser). Soil and debris observed in the cabinet below the iced tea dispenser. Clean often enough to prevent accumulation.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee in training was observed working at the 3 part sink and rinsed hands prior to heading to the microwave to check on food. Employee was then getting paper towels to dry hands and was advised on proper handwashing between tasks. Employee washed hands per inspector’s request prior to continuing to the next task.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Employee in training was observed rinsing hands at the 3 part sink. Proper handwashing at designated handwashing sink was discussed, and handwasing occurred prior to employee continuing with the next task.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Prep cooler was still soiled with general buildup of food splash on the inner surfaces of doors, on gaskets, and in the bottom of the unit. Food was placed in walk-in cooler during inspection to allow for proper cleaning. Ensure cleaning inside the prep cooler daily/as needed to eliminate buildup.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairs are scheduled to occur for tiles at and around the mop sink and the area behind the floor drain under the stainless steel prep sink where debris and moisture accumulation were observed during the routine inspection. The crew scheduled to provide repairs arrived during inspection. See general comments for additional information.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning has occurred since the routine inspection. Hood filters over the grill (and fryers) need additional cleaning and will be addressed when hoods are serviced in the near future. See general comments for additional information.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Several priority violations were observed during the inspection. See violations 8, 9, 15, & 16 for details. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the follow-up inspection. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 GM took the food manager course to earn certification in 2021 but did not have a copy of certification at the facility. Assistant manager was also present and had a copy of their current certification. GM is the designated person in charge and needs maintain a copy of manager certification on-site. 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 Signed copies of employee health reporting agreements were not on file for the assistant manager and two other employees working at the time of inspection. Employee health policy was discussed. Reporting agreements were signed for all staff that did not currently have one on file. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Employee was observed chewing gum while working on food prep. Gum was discarded at request of inspector. 
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee was observed behind the front service counter holding single use gloves in their hands. Employee had not yet washed their hands and was advised on handwashing prior to glove use. Employee washed their hands before putting on a new pair of gloves to continue with food prep.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, before putting on gloves and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 (B) Ice scoop was covered by ice in the bin of the ice machine. Manager put on a glove to remove the ice scoop. Ensure proper storage of the ice scoop with the handle up out of the ice if stored in the ice bin or in the designated ice scoop holder on the side of the ice machine. 
Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in ¶¶ (D) and (E) of this section, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Front handwashing sink was blocked upon arrival of inspector. A cup intended for cleaning the shake machine was in the basin, and a jacket was on the front ledge. Items were removed and proper use of handwashing sink was discussed. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items in the basin and/or on the front ledge of the handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee working at fryers was observed adjusting face mask with gloved hand. Employee then continued on to the next task without a glove change. Proper use of single use gloves was discussed with employee. Hands were washed prior to putting a new glove to continue with food prep. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 A soiled knife was observed in the crevice between the prep cooler and prep table on the make line. The crevice had buildup of debris accumulation. Knife was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. Crevices between equipment are not considered clean surfaces for storage of food contact surfaces. Cease the practice of storing knives in crevices located between pieces of equipment.  
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Can opener blade was soiled from use the previous operating day. None of the staff working at the time of inspection used the can open for morning prep. Can opener was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sani-bucket in the lobby was observed with a concentration less than 100ppm quat. Solution was old and left from the previous operating day. Assistant manager removed the solution from the lobby for disposal. Fresh sanitizer solutions at 200ppm were provided.
Ensure proper disposal os old sanitizer solution at the end of operations daily.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Thawed portions of vacuum packaged fish were observed in the walk-in cooler. Ensure packaging is at minimum cut open from the moment vacuum packaged fish is taken from the freezer to begin thawing in the walk-in cooler. 
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in ¶(A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in ¶ (B) of this section.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solutions were not available for use as prep was occurring. Sani-buckets were prepared at a concentration of 200ppm. Ensure sanitizer solution is setup and available for use prior to beginning prep and other operations. 
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Buildup of food splash was observed inside the prep cooler on the inner surfaces of door, on gaskets, and in the bottom of the unit. Ensure cleaning inside the prep cooler daily/as needed to eliminate buildup.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.citation_text:
6-501.18 Inner surface of toilet bowl up along the rim was soiled with buildup. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Plumbing fixtures such handwashing sinks, toilets, and urinals shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 1. Ponding water and debris were observed in between tiles with low grout around the mop sink. Moisture and debris accumulation were also observed in front of the mopsink where a piece of floor tile was missing.
2. Debris was observed around the floor drain beneath the stainless steel prep sink where tile was damaged. 
Provide proper repairs to the floor tiles in the aforementioned areas to allow for ease in cleaning and eliminate buildup of ponding liquid and debris.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 1. Wall under the 3 part sink was soiled with general buildup of splash.
2. Floor in dry storage area was soiled with spilled syrup splash around in-use soda syrup boxes. 
3. Wall and floor under/behind grill were soiled with grease. 
4. Hood filter over grill was soiled with grease buildup. 
Cleaning frequency was discussed.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 GM and another employee working at the time of inspection did not have a signed reporting agreement on file. Employee health policy was discussed, and copies of reporting agreement were signed during inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Paper towel was used to shut off the manual faucet prior to drying hands. GM was advised to revisit proper handwashing technique with all employees and ensure a barrier is used when shutting off the manual faucet as the last step of the handwashing process.
 Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet and to dispense paper towels would also be acceptable.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook was observed wiping down general surfaces and adjusting face mask prior to returning to the fryers to prepare an order. Handwashing was not observed prior to beginning food prep. Cook was advised on handwashing between tasks and after adjusting face masks. Cook washed hands prior to returning to food prep. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands should also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Pans of raw shrimp and raw fish were stored over hotdogs and dressing in the bottom holding area of the prep cooler. Foods were rearranged to allow for proper storage of raw animal foods below ready to eat foods. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.
-Box of bacon was open and top layer of bacon was uncovered in the walk-in cooler. Ensure foods are covered between uses in the walk-in cooler. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Corn was observed with an internal temperature of 79F in a hot holding unit. GM was unsure as to why the corn was in the warmer because it wasn’t turned on. Hot holding unit was turned on, and corn was discarded. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Open package of hotdogs in the bottom holding area of the prep cooler did not have a date mark. Employee stated the open package of hotdogs was removed from the walk-in cooler earlier today. Package was likely opened during the previous operating day. Product was dated and kept for use.  
Except as specified in ¶¶ (E) -(G) of this section, refrigerated, ready to eat TCS food prepared and packaged by a food processing plant shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in ¶ (A). The day the original container is opened in the food establishment shall be counted as Day 1, and the day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 Box of fish was observed on the floor in the walk-in freezer. Proper storage of food up off the floor in walk-in units was discussed. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food in a clean, dry location; where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Scoop for cole slaw was stored on top of the pan at the front counter cold holding unit. Employee placed the scoop in the container with the handle extended out.
-Scoop for rice was stored on top of a pan at the hot holding unit in back. Scoop was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
-Ladles for cheese sauce and chili were observed partially submerged in a small pan with water in the hot holding unit. Water was observed at 130F. Ladles and pan were taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in food with their handles above top of food and container. If water is used for storage of utensils between uses, the water must be maintained at a temperature of 135F/above.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Ponding water and debris were observed in between tiles with low grout around the mop sink.
-Ponding water and debris were observed around the floor drain beneath the mop sink where the tile was damaged. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 DISH AREA: Walls, attached plumbing, the floor, and floor drain were soiled with splash and general buildup beneath the 3 part sink.
COOK LINE: Wall and floor were soiled with grease behind the flat grill.
FRYERS: Floor was soiled with grease and food debris next to and behind the fryer across from the reach-in freezer. 
UNDER MOP SINK: Floor drain was soiled with general buildup. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 Two of the food employees working at the time of inspection did not have a signed reporting agreement on file. One employee just started today, while the other employee has been working with the organization for a week. PIC had both employees go over the health policy and sign a copy of the reporting agreement during the inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12 Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to touching the handle of paper towel dispenser to retrieve paper towels after handwashing process was completed. Proper technique was discussed with staff, and all employees were observed washing hands with proper technique for the remainder of inspection. 
 Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet and to dispense paper towels would also be acceptable.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook was observed getting a drink and did not was hands prior to continuing with various tasks, including getting wiping cloths for sani-buckets. Cook noted he was not immediately working with food. However, hands should always be washed after drinking from a personal beverage and prior to continuing with any tasks in the kitchen or service line. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands should also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-703.11 Equipment used for batter prep was washed, rinsed, and quickly dunked in sanitizer prior to removing to air dry during ware washing. Staff were advised on submersion in sanitizer for proper contact time of at minimum 30 seconds (or length of time indicated on product label) prior to removing to air dry. Equipment in question was placed back in sanitizer to allow for proper sanitization. 
 After being cleaned, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in chemical manual operations, including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114 (in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions). Contact time shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use instructions by providing at least 30 seconds for quaternary ammonia chemical sanitizing solutions.

4-601.11 Can opener blade was soiled with stuck on debris. Can opener was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Soda nozzles and diffusers had varying amounts of buildup. Ensure proper cleaning of nozzles and diffusers as needed to eliminate buildup. 
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Ice scoop holder insert was soiled with general buildup and debris. Cleaning frequency was discussed. Scoop and insert were cleaned and sanitized during inspection.  
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-201.11 An inverted pan was still in use as a leg at the two drawer cooler. Grease buildup was observed in the lip of the inverted pan and on the floor around the pan. Manager state a new table was ordered as of the last routine inspection. Until the table is replaced, clean the lip of the inverted pan and the floor around it daily/as needed to eliminate general buildup and food debris. 
Equipment and utensils shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-603.12 Fryer skimmer hanging in clean equipment storage was observed with stuck on food debris. Skimmer was removed for cleaning. 
--What appeared to be an old label for hotdogs was observed on a lid used to cover a pan of fish in the bottom of the prep cooler. The date appeared to say 2/6 but may have said 2/16 and been mistakenly placed on the fish. Cook removed the label and provided proper label for fish. Manager was advised to speak with staff about precleaning and repeating the steps of ware washing as many times as necessary to ensure removal of soil from all surfaces. Also, proper labeling and removal of labels during ware washing were discussed.
If necessary for effective cleaning, utensils and equipment shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The interior of cabinet to right of fry line was soiled with food debris and splash. The drain opening in cold holding area above the cabinet to the right of fry line was soiled with food debris. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.citation_text:
6-501.18 Inner surfaces of toilets were soiled with buildup from use. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Plumbing fixtures such handwashing sinks, toilets, and urinals shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Three part sink was not properly sealed to the wall. Old caulk has been removed from the 3 part sink last year and not replaced. Provide a proper seal. 
--Coving base tile to the right of the mop basin was damaged. Tile was said to be on the list of repairs as of the last routine inspection. Provide repairs.
--Caulk at mopsink is heavily molded and in disrepair. Replace the damaged moldy caulk. 
Note: GM indicated the mopsink was due to be replaced during previous routine inspection, at which time the coving to the right and the caulk would be addressed. 
--Hood filter over grill and ansul system had grease buildup. Clean the aforementioned surfaces.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
Floor, walls, ceilings and equipment should be maintained smooth, easily cleanable, and in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-303.11 One light bulb was burnt out above the grill, and the light shield of the other was soiled with grease accumulation and dead bugs inside. Clean the light shields and replace the burnt out light bulb.
The light intensity shall be at least 540 lux (50 foot candles) at a surface where a food employee is working with food or working with utensils or equipment where employee safety is a factor.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Food employees were observed washing hands without proper technique. A barrier was not used to shut off the manual faucet prior to retrieving paper towels to dry hands. The handle of the paper towel dispenser was also touched after handwashing process was completed. Proper technique was discussed with staff, and all employees were observed washing hands with proper technique for the remainder of inspection. Manager noted he also went over proper handwashing and will be re-training staff. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable if that is an option depending on the type of handle.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Can opener had buildup along the edge of the blade. Can opener was placed at 3 part sink for ware washing. 
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

Ice machine had a small amount of mold buildup on the ceiling behind the baffle. Cleaning frequency was discussed.
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Green beans in the walkin cooler had surface and internal temperatures at 52F and 54F-64F respectively. Prep time and date were 11:10am 8/26. Beans were removed from a can and placed in the walkin cooler for storage. It was 3:05pm when the temperatures were verified. Manager chose to discard two pans of green beans from the walkin cooler.
Coney sauce opened to be cold held around the same time today had an internal temperature of 53F and was moved to the freezer to help quickly drop the temperature.
Options for rapid chilling of foods prepared at ambient temperature were discussed, including pre-chilling products prior to use. 
Time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 4 hours to 41F/below if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.citation_text:
3-501.19 Hush puppy batter held at room temperature on the make line had a label containing time stamps of 930am (prep); 1030am (ready), and 1230pm (discard). Batter was observed on the make line after 230pm. Batter was removed for discard and fresh product was prepared. Manager was advised to ensure staff are monitoring the time and properly using or discarding batter within 4hrs as specified in their time control policy.
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours the food shall be used or discarded, within 4 hours from the point in time when the food was removed from temperature control.
Batters prepared and held at room temperature must be used or discarded within 4hrs from the time of preparation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled: 
A) shelving to the right inside the walkin cooler (mold and soil);
B)  interior of cabinet to right of fry line (food/splash);  and
C) two drawer holding table - pans and inner surfaces (breading/general buildup).

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Leaks were observed at the front service area handsink and the kitchen handsink. A technician from a local company was on-site to place a bid for multiple repairs at the time of inspection. The bid was approved for work to be done in the near future.
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Ceiling air return at make line was observed with dust buildup. Clean the air returns as needed to eliminate dust accumulation. 
Old caulk has been removed from the 3 part sink. Manager has caulk to provide proper seal. 
Coving base tile to the right of the mop basin was damaged. Manager noted the mopsink is going to be replaced in the near future. Repairs for the coving will occur at that time. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.


Floor, walls, ceilings and equipment should be maintained smooth, easily cleanable, and in good repair. Damaged equipment and materials should be replaced to prevent accumulation of soil, food, and to prevent the harborage of insects.
